title: DELETE Statement
description: Learn how to use the DELETE statement to remove one or more rows from a table.

data.text: To remove one or more rows from a table, use the DELETE statement. The WHERE clause specifies which rows to delete. Without a WHERE clause, all rows are deleted.

data.title: DELETE Syntax
data.content: Deletes rows from a table, optionally limiting by TOP and filtering with WHERE.

items: Specify the table name in the FROM clause from which rows will be deleted.
Use the TOP clause to delete a specific number or percentage of random rows.
Use the WHERE clause to specify which rows to delete. Rows where the condition evaluates to true are removed.
Without a WHERE clause, DELETE removes all rows from the table.

data.text: Delete a Number of Random Rows
The following DELETE statement removes 21 random rows from the product_history table.

data.title: DELETE TOP N Rows
data.content: Deletes 21 random rows from the product_history table.

data.text: SQL Server returns (21 rows affected), confirming the deletion.
Delete a Percent of Random Rows

data.title: DELETE TOP PERCENT Rows
data.content: Deletes 5 percent of random rows from the product_history table.

data.text: SQL Server returns (15 rows affected), which is 5% of the 300 rows in the table.
Use the WHERE clause to delete only rows that meet a specific condition. The following example removes all products with a model year of 2017.

data.title: DELETE with WHERE
data.content: Deletes all products from the year 2017.

data.text: Delete All Rows from a Table
To remove all rows from a table, use DELETE without a WHERE clause. However, for large tables, TRUNCATE TABLE is faster and more efficient.

data.title: DELETE All Rows
data.content: Removes all rows from the product_history table.

data.title: Tip
data.text: For removing all rows from a large table, prefer TRUNCATE TABLE over DELETE without a WHERE clause. TRUNCATE is faster and uses fewer system resources.

data.title: DELETE Key Points
points: Use DELETE FROM with a WHERE clause to remove specific rows.
Use DELETE TOP (N) to delete a specific number of random rows.
Use DELETE TOP (N) PERCENT to delete a percentage of random rows.
Without a WHERE clause, DELETE removes all rows.
For large tables, TRUNCATE TABLE is more efficient than DELETE without WHERE.
